summary: Exemestane is an irreversible steroidal aromatase inactivator ('suicide inhibitor') structurally related to androstenedione, used in postmenopausal women with estrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer. It is indicated for adjuvant treatment in women who have had 2-3 years of tamoxifen and are switched to complete 5 years of hormonal therapy, and for advanced disease that has progressed on tamoxifen. The dose is 25 mg once daily after a meal (50 mg with strong CYP3A4 inducers). Key risks are bone loss/fractures and fetal harm.
indications: Adjuvant treatment of postmenopausal women with estrogen-receptor-positive early breast cancer who have received 2-3 years of tamoxifen, switched to exemestane to complete 5 consecutive years of hormonal therapy
Treatment of advanced breast cancer in postmenopausal women whose disease has progressed following tamoxifen therapy

admin: Take one 25 mg tablet once daily after a meal at about the same time each day
Confirm postmenopausal status before and, where appropriate, during treatment
Verify pregnancy status in females of reproductive potential before starting
Increase to 50 mg daily if a strong CYP3A4 inducer is co-administered
Support bone health with calcium, vitamin D and weight-bearing exercise
moa: In postmenopausal women, the principal source of circulating estrogens is aromatase-mediated conversion of adrenal and ovarian androgens (androstenedione and testosterone) to estrone and estradiol in peripheral tissues. Exemestane is a steroidal aromatase inactivator structurally related to the natural substrate androstenedione; it acts as a false substrate, is processed to an intermediate that binds irreversibly to and inactivates the aromatase enzyme ('suicide inhibition'). This significantly lowers circulating estrogens without detectable effect on adrenal corticosteroid or aldosterone biosynthesis, depriving estrogen-dependent tumors of their growth stimulus.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to exemestane or any excipient
Premenopausal women / women who are or may become pregnant
relative: Pre-existing osteoporosis or low bone mineral density
monitor: Hepatic and renal function as clinically indicated

preg: Contraindicated. Based on animal data and mechanism, exemestane can cause fetal harm (embryo-fetal toxicity, abortion, prolonged/abnormal labor in animals). Verify pregnancy status before starting and advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception; the indicated population is postmenopausal women.
lact: Do not breastfeed during treatment and for a period after the last dose, due to potential for serious adverse effects in a nursing infant.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required for renal impairment, although systemic exposure is increased.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is routinely required for hepatic impairment, although systemic exposure is increased; the increase remains within the well-tolerated single-dose range.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, St. John's wort) - reduce exemestane levels; increase dose to 50 mg daily
Estrogen-containing agents (including hormone replacement) - antagonize the action of exemestane; do not co-administer
moderate: Other endocrine breast-cancer therapies - no established benefit to combining; avoid
Drugs affecting bone metabolism - additive effect on bone density
minor: CYP3A4 inhibitors - modest increase in exposure; no dose change required
interactions.food: Take after a meal; food increases absorption (bioavailability rises ~40% with high-fat meals).
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; it can worsen hot flushes and contribute to bone loss.
interactions.diagnostics: Lowers serum estradiol; may modestly alter lipids and liver enzymes; reduces bone mineral density over time.

monitoring: Bone mineral density at baseline and periodically
Serum vitamin D (correct deficiency before/during therapy)
Liver function tests if symptoms arise
counsel: Take one tablet once a day after food, at about the same time each day
Hot flushes and joint aches are common - report if severe or limiting
Protect your bones: take calcium and vitamin D, do weight-bearing exercise; bone density will be checked
Do not use estrogen products (including HRT) with this medicine
Report severe tiredness, yellowing of skin/eyes, chest pain or breathlessness, or signs of an allergic reaction
pk: Maximal estrogen suppression within a few days of dosing
Peak plasma at ~1.2 h (fed); absorption increased by food
Irreversible enzyme inactivation sustains estrogen suppression with once-daily dosing
Store at 20-25 C; protect from light and moisture
pearls: Steroidal aromatase INACTIVATOR (suicide inhibitor) - distinct from non-steroidal anastrozole/letrozole
For POSTMENOPAUSAL women with ER-positive disease only
Take AFTER a meal - food significantly increases absorption
Increase to 50 mg daily when given with a strong CYP3A4 inducer
Bone loss is a key long-term risk - monitor BMD and ensure vitamin D/calcium adequacy
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not take two tablets at once.
overdose: There is no specific antidote; doses far above therapeutic (single doses up to 800 mg, and 600 mg daily for weeks) were well tolerated. Manage with general supportive care, frequent monitoring of vital signs and close observation; treat symptomatically.
